FINDING_ID: IM_F002
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83
DESCRIPTION: FIND: The compatibility shim breaks the cross-subsystem API contract around FSM typing by exporting concrete FSM types `State` and `Event` from `_types`, while the only visible contract for the immune integration describes `fsm.select_event(...) -> str` and `fsm.transition(event: str) -> str`. This is not the same issue as merely “the summary omits State/Event”; the cross-cutting defect is that the public shim presents typed FSM enums/classes as part of the stable surface, while the orchestration interface summary specifies stringly-typed behaviour for the exact immune integration path (`process_round()`). That creates an ownership mismatch across `_types`, `_fsm`, and `_manager`: callers using shim-exported `Event`/`State` cannot know whether immune integration consumes enums or raw strings. Evidence: Artifact 1 explicitly re-exports `State` and `Event`; Interface Summary Section 1 explicitly declares `fsm.select_event(...) -> str` and `fsm.transition(event) -> str`. Those contracts conflict.  
FIX: Normalize the public contract to typed FSM values and update the interface summary text accordingly:
<<<<
| `fsm.select_event(conv, dim, crit, complete)` | `(bool, bool, bool, bool) → str` | FSM event selection from round outcomes |
| `fsm.transition(event)` | `(str) → str` | FSM state transition, returns new state |
====
| `fsm.select_event(conv, dim, crit, complete)` | `(bool, bool, bool, bool) → Event` | FSM event selection from round outcomes |
| `fsm.transition(event)` | `(Event) → State` | FSM state transition, returns new state |
>>>>
FOLLOW: If this fix is applied, `_manager.process_round()` must pass/receive `Event` and `State` consistently, not raw strings. Any event logging via `ManagerEvent`, any persistence in `RoundResult.state`, and any tests asserting string values will need explicit `.value` conversion or updated typing. If `_fsm` is actually string-based internally, then the alternative fix is to stop exporting `State`/`Event` from the shim; but one of these contracts must change because both cannot be true simultaneously. VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003
SEVERITY: 0.71
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79
DESCRIPTION: FIND: The shim exposes a cross-subsystem private dependency as if it were part of the supported API: `_finding_similarity`, `_tokenize_for_similarity`, `_bigrams`, and `_STOPWORDS` are re-exported from `_convergence`, while the immune integration contract explicitly depends on `convergence_detector._novel_classes(r)`, another private member. The missed issue is not just “private helpers are exported”; it is that both sides of the convergence/immune boundary are relying on private implementation details, so the boundary is structurally unstable in two directions. Evidence: Artifact 1 publicly re-exports underscore-prefixed convergence helpers. Interface Summary Section 1 says `process_round()` calls `convergence_detector._novel_classes(r)`. That indicates immune orchestration is coupled to convergence internals rather than a stable public method.  
FIX: Replace private-method use with a public convergence API and stop exporting private convergence helpers from the shim:
<<<<
from bench.dm._convergence import (  # noqa: F401
    ConvergenceDetector,
    _finding_similarity,
    _tokenize_for_similarity,
    _bigrams,
    _STOPWORDS,
)
====
from bench.dm._convergence import ConvergenceDetector  # noqa: F401
>>>>
and update the interface contract text:
<<<<
| `convergence_detector._novel_classes(r)` | `(int) → Set` | Returns flaw classes new in round r |
====
| `convergence_detector.novel_classes(r)` | `(int) → Set` | Returns flaw classes new in round r |
>>>>
FOLLOW: This requires `_convergence.py` to provide a public `novel_classes()` wrapper or rename the existing method, and `_manager.process_round()` must call that public method. Any tests or external tooling using the shim-exported underscore helpers will break and should be migrated to public APIs. This also tightens the convergence/immune ownership boundary: convergence owns similarity internals; immune consumes only public novelty outputs. VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F004
SEVERITY: 0.63
FLAW_CLASS: 8
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: FIND: The shim’s module inventory assigns immune detection ownership too narrowly: `_immune.py             DetectorHealthMonitor (immune detection layer)`. But the stated analytical boundary and the exported surface show immune diagnosis is split across `_types` (`DetectorDiagnosis`), `_immune` (`DetectorHealthMonitor`), `_failure_handler` (`FailureHandler`, `CorrelatedFailureModel`), and `_manager` (`_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`, `apply_diagnosis`, `_apply_transform`, `process_round`). The missed defect is an architectural misframing: the docstring describes the immune subsystem as if `_immune.py` alone were “the immune detection layer,” while actual diagnosis/remediation ownership spans four modules. Evidence: Artifact 1 inventory line for `_immune.py`; export lines for `DetectorDiagnosis`, `FailureHandler`, `CorrelatedFailureModel`, and `DynamicManager`; task boundary includes remediation and integration methods outside `_immune.py`.  
FIX: Correct the module-ownership inventory text:
<<<<
    _immune.py             DetectorHealthMonitor (immune detection layer)
    _failure_handler.py    FailureHandler, CorrelatedFailureModel
    _events.py             ManagerEventStream
    _manager.py            DynamicManager (orchestrator, _REMEDIATION_CHAINS,
                           apply_diagnosis, _apply_transform, process_round)
====
    _immune.py             DetectorHealthMonitor (immune monitoring/diagnosis)
    _failure_handler.py    FailureHandler, CorrelatedFailureModel (immune failure classification/recovery)
    _events.py             ManagerEventStream
    _manager.py            DynamicManager (immune remediation integration:
                           _REMEDIATION_CHAINS, apply_diagnosis, _apply_transform, process_round)
>>>>
FOLLOW: This documentation fix changes no runtime behaviour, but it affects how reviewers, maintainers, and downstream users reason about ownership. It also exposes a downstream gap in the current interface summary: the immune subsystem should be documented as spanning diagnosis, failure handling, remediation application, and round-level integration, not as a single-module feature. VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F005
SEVERITY: 0.61
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73
DESCRIPTION: FIND: The interface surface for immune configuration is underspecified at the exact point where the immune subsystem mutates other subsystems’ stopping criteria. The shim exports only `DynamicManagementConfig`, while the interface summary lists mutable fields `tau_sim`, `tau_vocab_growth`, `per_model_directives`, `pre_decompose_models`, and several immune thresholds. However, no typed or documented sub-API distinguishes immune-owned config from convergence-owned or prompt-owned config. This is a cross-cutting completeness defect: `_manager.apply_diagnosis()` can mutate convergence and prompting behaviour through a generic config bag without a declared stable sub-interface. Evidence: Artifact 1 exports only `DynamicManagementConfig`; Interface Summary Section 2 lists immune writes to `tau_sim`, `tau_vocab_growth`, `per_model_directives`, `pre_decompose_models`; Section 3 lists immune parameters; no dedicated immune-config type or subsection is exported.  
FIX: Make the immune-owned config surface explicit in the shim/module docs by documenting the immune fields under `DynamicManagementConfig`:
<<<<
    _types.py              Config, enums, dataclasses (all shared vocabulary)
====
    _types.py              Config, enums, dataclasses (all shared vocabulary,
                           including immune config fields:
                           immune_feedback_enabled, immune_damping_rounds,
                           max_per_model_directive_chars, timeout_multiplier,
                           theta_under, n_fail, persistence_window,
                           eta_underperform, k_min, tau_sim, tau_vocab_growth,
                           per_model_directives, pre_decompose_models)
>>>>
FOLLOW: This is documentation/interface repair, not a behavioural fix. Downstream, tests and callers that treat `DynamicManagementConfig` as an opaque bag remain possible, but the ownership boundary becomes explicit: convergence thresholds and prompt directives are mutable by immune logic. If the implementation intends these fields to be internal-only, then the opposite fix is needed: stop advertising them as part of the public compatibility surface. VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F006
SEVERITY: 0.58
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64
DESCRIPTION: FIND: The public shim exports `ManagerEventStream` separately from the immune layer, while the immune boundary includes `FailureHandler` calling `event_callback(event)` with `ManagerEvent`. The missed cross-cutting issue is ownership ambiguity of event emission semantics: the immune subsystem depends on eventing for failure handling, but the shim/documentation present `_events.py` as orthogonal rather than as part of the immune execution path. This is not the already-noted “relationship undocumented” issue alone; it is a packaging/interface defect because a backward-compatible API should group or document runtime-coupled components together. Evidence: Artifact 1 has separate sections “Immune layer” and “Event stream”; Interface Summary Section 1 lists `event_callback(event)` under “From FailureHandler (within boundary, calls config)”; Section 4 lists `ManagerEvent` and `ManagerEventType` as immune-boundary types.  
FIX: Amend the shim section header/comments to reflect the runtime dependency:
<<<<
# ── Immune layer ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from bench.dm._immune import DetectorHealthMonitor  # noqa: F401
from bench.dm._failure_handler import (  # noqa: F401
    FailureHandler,
    CorrelatedFailureModel,
)

# ── Event stream ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from bench.dm._events import ManagerEventStream  # noqa: F401
====
# ── Immune layer and supporting event interface ──────────────────────────
from bench.dm._immune import DetectorHealthMonitor  # noqa: F401
from bench.dm._failure_handler import (  # noqa: F401
    FailureHandler,
    CorrelatedFailureModel,
)
from bench.dm._events import ManagerEventStream  # noqa: F401
>>>>
FOLLOW: No runtime impact from the comment/import regrouping itself. The downstream implication is documentation alignment: `ManagerEvent`, `ManagerEventType`, and `ManagerEventStream` should be referenced in the immune interface summary as supporting dependencies of `FailureHandler`, not as a detached subsystem. If the project wants stricter separation, then `FailureHandler` should accept a narrower logger/protocol interface instead of direct event-stream coupling. VERIFIED: TRUE
